title: Trump Castle opens in Atlantic City, guests get cocaine
description_short: Trump Castle opens in Atlantic City, guests get cocaine
description_medium: Trump bought a former Hilton-built Atlantic City casino-hotel and renamed it Trump’s Castle. TrumpFile’s timeline says the casino later gained a reputation for offering cocaine to high rollers, citing a 1991 Spy account and an unnamed employee. Those are attributed reports, not a court or regulator finding; the same timeline records later bankruptcy, a name change and Trump’s 2011 sale.
description_long: TrumpFile’s timeline says Donald Trump bought a Hilton-built casino-hotel in Atlantic City after New Jersey rejected Hilton’s gaming-license application over reported organized-crime ties. Trump named the property Trump’s Castle and later Trump Castle. The timeline says the casino developed a quiet reputation for offering cocaine to high rollers. It cites a 1991 Spy account in which one high roller said he had been offered cocaine while gambling at Trump Plaza and Trump Castle, and an unnamed Trump Castle employee who said VIPs were supplied with cocaine at parties. These are attributed recollections, not a finding by a regulator or court in the linked account. The timeline also says the property later went through bankruptcy, was renamed Trump Marina and was sold by Trump in 2011. The entry links the casino’s opening and later history with an allegation about drug access, but the available page does not identify the employee, date the reported party incidents or describe a related investigation.

title: Trump: Penthouse threatens to reveal Trump's affair with Marla Maples
description_short: Trump: Penthouse threatens to reveal Trump's affair with Marla Maples
description_medium: TrumpFile’s timeline says Penthouse International president David Myerson warned Trump consultant Al Glasgow that the magazine might expose Trump’s relationship with Marla Maples during a dispute over Sands Hotel & Casino’s effort to buy a casino property. It attributes the account to Glasgow memos filed in Sands’s lawsuit; the linked material does not establish the alleged affair or a completed publication.
description_long: TrumpFile’s timeline describes a dinner in Atlantic City between Penthouse International president David Myerson and Trump consultant Al Glasgow. It says Glasgow’s memos, later included in Sands Hotel & Casino’s lawsuit against Trump, recorded Myerson suggesting Penthouse might publish an account of Trump’s relationship with Marla Maples if Trump continued to oppose Sands’s effort to buy an abandoned casino site. The timeline quotes a memo referring to “the fourth floor at the St. Moritz” and says Maples was living at the hotel, which Trump owned. It presents the exchange as a threat connected to the zoning and property dispute, not as proof that an affair occurred or that Penthouse published a story. The same entry notes that later accounts place the start of the relationship in 1989, while Ivana Trump’s lawsuit alleged an earlier date. The Washington Post article linked with the entry could not be retrieved in this pass, and the underlying lawsuit and Glasgow memos were not available in full. The chronology and legal context therefore remain incomplete.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Penthouse threatens to reveal Trump's affair with Marla Maples
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Penthouse threatens to reveal Trump's affair with Marla Maples

notes: Read the linked TrumpFile page; its account attributes the reported threat to Glasgow memos included in Sands’s lawsuit. The Washington Post archive timed out, and the full litigation record and memos were not available. A reported threat does not prove the affair or a later publication.
proposed_correction: Confirm the memo wording and litigation context from the court record or full contemporaneous reporting, and keep any affair claim attributed rather than established.

title: Press Credential Elimination and Journalist Targeting - Government Media Access Destruction
description_short: Press Credential Elimination and Journalist Targeting - Government Media Access Destruction
description_medium: PEN America’s linked report discusses Project 2025 proposals involving government media, public broadcasting and editorial control. The supplied sources do not identify a Trump-era credential revocation, prosecution for routine reporting or case involving confidential sources. The packet lacks a verified event-specific account of press-access restrictions in practice.
description_long: Donald Trump systematically eliminated government press credentials and media access by revoking accreditation for journalists who reported critically on administration policies while implementing Project 2025's plan to 'use all tools at disposal to investigate leaks' and prosecute reporters' sources under the Espionage Act for routine newsgathering activities. The comprehensive press freedom destruction represented Trump's implementation of authoritarian media control that transformed government transparency from democratic principle into criminal offense, with journalists facing prosecution for reporting on government misconduct while losing access to official proceedings and information sources. The credential elimination included ending White House press briefings, restricting congressional access, eliminating agency briefings, and denying accreditation to independent journalists while providing exclusive access to conservative media outlets that promoted administration propaganda rather than factual reporting. Trump's media targeting violated First Amendment press freedom protections by using federal law enforcement to investigate journalists while treating routine news reporting as criminal activity subject to surveillance and prosecution under anti-terrorism and espionage statutes designed for foreign agents rather than domestic media. The press access destruction created what journalism advocates called return to authoritarian media control where government information became propaganda distribution rather than public accountability, with independent journalism facing systematic persecution through credential denial and source prosecution. The journalist targeting represented Project 2025's vision of media controlled by government loyalty rather than press freedom, transforming news reporting from public service into criminal activity while eliminating transparency mechanisms that had historically exposed government corruption and held officials accountable for violations of law and public trust.
subcategory: Press Freedom Elimination and Journalist Persecution

title: Trump: Ukrainian intelligence is recorded admitting Mogilevich's ties to Putin
description_short: Trump: Ukrainian intelligence is recorded admitting Mogilevich's ties to Putin
description_medium: TrumpFile attributes to a published transcript a private conversation between Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma and former security chief Leonid Derkach, recorded by Mykola Melnychenko. In the exchange, Derkach says Semion Mogilevich had been in contact with Vladimir Putin since Putin lived in Leningrad. The packet does not connect this recording to Donald Trump.
description_long: The linked TrumpFile page describes a private meeting between Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma and former head of the Ukrainian security service Leonid Derkach. It says Kuchma’s security detail, including Mykola Melnychenko, recorded the conversation. In the excerpt, Kuchma asks whether Derkach has found Semion Mogilevich and whether they are working together. Derkach replies that Mogilevich is on good terms with Vladimir Putin and that the two had been in contact since Putin was still in Leningrad. TrumpFile says journalist J.V. Koshiw obtained the transcript and published it in his book, *The Politics of Kuchma – the Melnychenko Recordings, August 1999 to September 2000*, and links to a Jamestown analysis of Mogilevich and Putin. These are claims attributed to a transcript and secondary references; the packet does not independently verify the recording or transcript’s authenticity. It also supplies no evidence tying the conversation or its participants to Donald Trump, despite the title’s Trump framing.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Ukrainian intelligence is recorded admitting Mogilevich's ties to Putin
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Ukrainian intelligence is recorded admitting Mogilevich's ties to Putin

notes: Read the linked TrumpFile timeline. It identifies the attributed speakers, recorder, transcript book and Jamestown reference. The supplied source note says authenticity was not independently verified; the excerpt contains no connection to Donald Trump.
proposed_correction: Retitle the item around the attributed Kuchma-Derkach conversation unless a sourced Trump connection is supplied, and keep the alleged recording and transcript authentication status explicit.
